elements.reason: The abstract text does not explicitly identify the report as a systematic review; this appears only in the article title, not in the abstract itself.

elements.quote: this paper updates and summarizes the current evidence informing rehabilitation of patients with coVid-19 and/or describing the consequences of the disease and its treatment.
elements.reason: The abstract's introduction clearly states the main objective of the review.

elements.quote: studies published from May 1 st to June 30 th , 2021 were selected, excluding descriptive studies and expert opinions.
elements.reason: Inclusion (publication window, study types) and exclusion criteria (descriptive studies, expert opinions) are stated in the abstract.

elements.quote: studies published from May 1 st to June 30 th , 2021 were selected
elements.reason: The abstract reports when studies were published/selected but does not name the information sources (databases) searched or when each was last searched.

elements.quote: we improved the quality assessment using the Joanna briggs institute checklists for observational studies and the cochrane risk of bias tool for randomized-controlled clinical trials (rcts).
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the risk of bias assessment methods for both observational studies and RCTs.

elements.quote: papers were categorized according to study design, research question, coVid-19 phase, limitations of functioning of rehabilitation interest, and type of rehabilitation service involved.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the methods used to categorize and synthesize the results (narrative categorization under 'Evidence synthesis').

elements.quote: Twenty-five, out of 3699 papers, were included. They were three RCTs, 13 cross-sectional studies and nine cohort studies.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies and summarizes study design characteristics, though participant numbers per study are not aggregated.

elements.quote: Twenty studies reported data on symptom prevalence (N.=13) or disease natural history (N.=7); and five studies reported intervention effectiveness at the individual level.
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes main outcome categories with numbers of studies, but does not report actual result estimates for the outcomes.

elements.quote: This third edition still provides a narrative synthesis of findings, as a meta-analysis is not applicable due to the high heterogeneity of the studies.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted, so no summary estimate with confidence interval can be reported in the abstract.
No comparative group analysis with a directional effect is reported in the abstract; the review used a narrative synthesis without group comparisons.

elements.quote: the most frequent risks of bias for rcts concerned weaknesses in allocation concealment, blinding of therapists, and lack of intention-to-treat analysis. Most analytical studies failed to identify or deal with confounders, describe or deal with dropouts or eventually perform an appropriate statistical analysis
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes key limitations of the included evidence, including risk of bias and methodological weaknesses.

elements.quote: There is a need for good quality intervention efficacy and effectiveness studies to complement the rapidly expanding evidence from observational studies.
elements.reason: The conclusions provide a general interpretation of the findings and their implications for future research.
The abstract does not mention any funding source for the review.
The abstract does not report registration (PROSPERO CRD42021181202 appears only in the main text, not in the abstract).

elements.quote: A high proportion of SARS-CoV-2 patients survive infection but the prevalence of chronic sequelae and resulting disability is increasing... To date, the ClinicalTrials.gov website 2 of the National Library of Medicine has registered more than 6400 clinical studies targeting the epidemiology and management of COVID-19, but only 245 studies (188 of which are ongoing) address rehabilitation in COVID-19 survivors. ... Most studies provided low-level descriptive evidence
elements.reason: The introduction describes the current state of knowledge (growing chronic sequelae/disability, predominance of low-level descriptive evidence, few rehabilitation studies) and highlights uncertainties such as the lack of high-quality intervention studies.

elements.quote: The best available research evidence is required to inform management and rehabilitation decisions, interventions, and health systems for COVID-19 survivors with adverse clinical sequelae. Further evidence is warranted to estimate the resources needed to plan for setting appropriate and adequately delivered post-acute and long-term rehabilitation services.
elements.reason: The need and importance of the review are explicitly explained: best evidence is required to inform rehabilitation decisions and service planning for COVID-19 survivors.

elements.quote: The methodology of this systematic review updates the second edition published in June 2020. 4
elements.reason: As an update (third edition) of an existing living review, the manuscript identifies and cites the previous review editions (second edition cited with reference 4) and explains the reason for updating (new analytical studies enabling critical appraisal, longer follow-up data).

The review includes studies on intervention effectiveness (five intervention studies, three RCTs), but no proposed mechanism of action of rehabilitation interventions is described anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

Rehabilitation for COVID-19 is a complex intervention delivered across multiple phases and settings, but no logic model or hypothesized relationships between intervention components and outcomes is reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: this paper updates and summarizes the current evidence informing rehabilitation of patients with coVid-19 and/or describing the consequences of the disease and its treatment.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the review's objective: to update and summarize evidence on rehabilitation of COVID-19 patients and the consequences of the disease and its treatment.

elements.quote: papers were categorized according to study design, research question, coVid-19 phase, limitations of functioning of rehabilitation interest, and type of rehabilitation service involved.
elements.reason: Although the review includes intervention effectiveness studies (five studies on intervention efficacy), no planned comparisons are stated in PICO format or any explicit comparison framework; only broad categorization criteria are mentioned.

elements.quote: The database search was conducted on July 2 nd , 2021 covering publication dates between May 1st and June 30 th , 2021. The search strategy, screening, and data extraction criteria were not changed from the previous edition 4 except for the exclusion of case reports and case series... we classified study designs according to the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
elements.reason: Some eligibility characteristics are given (publication dates, exclusion of case reports/series, study design classification) but full study characteristics (population, interventions, settings, outcome criteria) are not explicitly specified in the retrieved evidence; the abstract adds exclusion of descriptive studies and expert opinions but the criteria remain incomplete.

elements.quote: covering publication dates between May 1st and June 30 th , 2021
elements.reason: Dissemination year/date range is specified, but no language or publication status criteria are reported.
No evidence distinguishes exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: Table III.- Distribution of studies by research question and study design... Epidemiology: Clinical presentation; Prevalence; Natural history, determining and modifying factors; Micro-level: individuals; Meso-level: health services; Macro-level: health systems
elements.reason: The grouping of studies for the syntheses is specified by research question (epidemiological vs individual intervention level) and study design, matching the review's stated aims of describing prevalence, natural history, and intervention effectiveness.

elements.quote: In this third edition, one modification was introduced to the selection criteria to narrow the breadth of findings and increase the level of evidence sought by excluding case reports and case series.
elements.reason: A rationale is provided for the notable restriction (exclusion of case reports and case series) to narrow breadth of findings and increase level of evidence.

elements.quote: The database search was conducted on July 2 nd , 2021 covering publication dates between May 1st and June 30 th , 2021.
elements.reason: A last-search date is reported for the database search, but since the names of all sources searched are not enumerated (e2), it is unclear whether dates for every source/other source consulted were reported.
No evidence names the bibliographic databases searched, their platforms, or coverage dates; the manuscript only refers generically to 'the databases'.
No study register, regulatory database, or online repository searched for studies is reported (PROSPERO is mentioned only as protocol registration, not a study search source).
No website or online search source used to identify studies is reported; the ClinicalTrials.gov and REH-COVER website mentions are contextual, not reported search sources.
No organisations or manufacturers contacted to identify studies are named in the retrieved evidence.
No individuals contacted to identify studies are described in the retrieved evidence.
No examination of reference lists is reported in the retrieved evidence.
No backward or forward citation searching is reported in the retrieved evidence.
No journals or conference proceedings consulted directly for studies are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The database search was conducted on July 2nd, 2021 covering publication dates between May 1st and June 30th, 2021. The search strategy, screening, and data extraction criteria were not changed from the previous edition
elements.reason: The manuscript states only the search dates and that the strategy was unchanged from a previous edition; no full search strategy (search strings, databases searched) is presented in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: covering publication dates between May 1st and June 30th, 2021... except for the exclusion of case reports and case series
elements.reason: Search limits (date range, exclusion of case reports/series) are described, but they are not explicitly justified by reference to the eligibility criteria beyond a general rationale in the discussion.

elements.quote: The search strategy, screening, and data extraction criteria were not changed from the previous edition
elements.reason: The search approach is based on a previously published edition (cited as reference 4), but the published strategy itself and any adaptations (beyond exclusion of case reports/series) are not detailed.
No mention of natural-language processing or text-analysis tools for identifying or refining search terms.
No mention of tools used to translate search strings between sources.
No description of any validation of the search strategy.
No description of peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS).
The manuscript does not describe the conceptual structure of the search (e.g., whether PICO-based) or how it was developed.

elements.quote: The search strategy, screening, and data extraction criteria were not changed from the previous edition 4 except for the exclusion of case reports and case series.
elements.reason: The methods state screening criteria were unchanged from a prior edition but nowhere report how many reviewers screened records at title/abstract or full-text stages.

elements.quote: Two review authors (C.A., V.I.) independently appraised the quality of studies and resolved disagreements by consensus
elements.reason: Independence is reported only for quality appraisal, not for the screening/selection process. No statement indicates whether screening was done independently.

elements.quote: resolved disagreements by consensus; in the case of persistent disagreement, a third review author was consulted (P.C.)
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution is described only for quality appraisal, not for study selection/screening; text_6 mentions managing design-classification discrepancies but not screening disagreement resolution.
No evidence that authors sought or needed additional eligibility information from study investigators; no such process is reported.
No mention of non-English records or translation of abstracts/articles for eligibility assessment.
No automation tools are reported as being used in the selection process.
No externally derived classifiers are mentioned in the manuscript.
No internally derived classifiers are mentioned in the manuscript.
No machine-learning prioritisation tools or screening stopping rules are reported.
No crowdsourcing platforms are mentioned.

No previously screened datasets used to eliminate records are described; the review states the search strategy and screening were unchanged from the prior edition but does not describe reuse of a previously screened dataset to remove records.
No evidence reports how many reviewers collected/extracted data from each report; the manuscript only states data extraction criteria were unchanged from the previous edition.
Independence is reported only for quality appraisal ('Two review authors (C.A., V.I.) independently appraised the quality of studies'), not for data collection/extraction.

elements.quote: Two review authors (C.A., V.I.) independently appraised the quality of studies and resolved disagreements by consensus; in the case of persistent disagreement, a third review author was consulted (P.C.)
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution is described only for quality appraisal, not for the data collection process, so the element as scoped to data collection is not reported.
No processes for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators are mentioned anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No automation tools used for data collection are described in the retrieved evidence.
No methods for translating articles for data collection are reported.
No software for extracting data from figures is specified.
No decision rules for selecting data from multiple reports of the same study or resolving inconsistencies among reports are described.

The methods do not list or define outcome domains for which data were sought. Only broad research question categories (prevalence, natural history, intervention efficacy) appear in tables/results, not a defined list of outcomes.
No time frame of outcome measurement is specified in the methods; mentions of follow-up periods appear only as descriptions of included studies, not as defined outcome time frames.
The manuscript does not state whether all compatible results within each outcome domain (all measures, time points, analyses) were sought.
Applies only if not all compatible results were sought; no selection process is reported and no evidence indicates such a process existed.
No changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance are reported; the only stated change was exclusion of case reports/case series (study selection, not outcomes).
No processes for selecting results within outcome domains are described, so no changes to such processes could be reported.
The manuscript does not identify outcomes considered most important for interpreting conclusions or provide a rationale for prioritisation.

elements.quote: papers were categorized according to study design, research question, coVid-19 phase, limitations of functioning of rehabilitation interest, and type of rehabilitation service involved.
elements.reason: The abstract and results (Tables I-III) indicate categories of data collected (study design, research question, COVID-19 phase, LFRI, rehabilitation setting, geographical area), but these variables are not formally listed and defined in the Methods as data items sought; no explicit data extraction variable list is provided.

No description of assumptions made about missing or unclear study information appears in the retrieved evidence. The only related note concerns study design classification, but no assumptions about missing/unclear data are reported.

No tool used to determine which data items to collect is cited; only quality appraisal tools (JBI checklists, Cochrane RoB) and an AHRQ study-design classification are mentioned, none of which addresses data item selection.

elements.quote: We also expanded the evaluation of the quality of evidence using JBI checklists 8 to appraise the methodological quality of observational studies and the Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool (RoB 1) to appraise methodological quality for randomized-controlled clinical trials (RCTs).
elements.reason: Both tools (JBI checklists for observational studies and Cochrane RoB 1 for RCTs) are explicitly named.

elements.quote: Figure 2.-Distribution of Risks of Bias in the included Randomized Controlled trials, according to the Cochrane Risk of Bias (RoB 1) tool.
elements.reason: The Figure 2 image (chunk text_8) displays RoB 1 domains (selection bias, performance bias, detection bias, attrition bias, reporting bias, other bias). JBI checklist items are only partially indicated (confounders, dropouts, statistical analysis in text_7 and Figure 3 caption), not fully enumerated.
No evidence reports whether an overall risk-of-bias judgement was made or the rules used to derive it.

elements.quote: using JBI checklists 8 to appraise the methodological quality of observational studies and the Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool (RoB 1)
elements.reason: Standard tools were used as named; no adaptations are reported or implied.

elements.quote: using JBI checklists 8 ... and the Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool (RoB 1)
elements.reason: Only existing published tools were used; no new tool was developed.

elements.quote: Two review authors (C.A., V.I.) independently appraised the quality of studies and resolved disagreements by consensus; in the case of persistent disagreement, a third review author was consulted (P.C.) and the disagreement resolved by consensus.
elements.reason: Number of reviewers, independent assessment, and disagreement-resolution procedures are fully reported.
No evidence of any process to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias information from study investigators; the requirement does not appear to apply.
No automation tools for risk-of-bias assessment are mentioned anywhere in the evidence.

No evidence specifies effect measures (e.g., risk ratio, mean difference) for any outcome. The review describes a narrative synthesis only: 'we evaluated 120 studies and included 25 in the narrative synthesis' (text_5), and 'metasynthesis was not possible due to study heterogeneity' (text_14), but no effect measure is named anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect size, nor their rationale, are reported in the retrieved evidence.
No methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure are described; the synthesis is purely narrative with no quantitative synthesis reported.
No effect measure is specified at all, so no justification for a choice of effect measure is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: papers were categorized according to study design, research question, coVid-19 phase, limitations of functioning of rehabilitation interest, and type of rehabilitation service involved... Additionally, to manage discrepancies encountered in past editions between the study design declared by authors and the actual design of the study, we classified study designs according to the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality 7 (Supplementary Digital Material 1: Supplementary Text File 1).
elements.reason: The review describes how studies were categorized by design and research question (Tables I-III synthesize distribution by research question and design, e.g. Table III), and mentions a classification scheme for study design, but it does not explicitly describe the process for deciding which studies were eligible for each synthesis (e.g. tabulating intervention characteristics and comparing against planned synthesis groups). Eligibility assignment to syntheses is only implied through the categorization tables and narrative synthesis description.

The retrieved evidence describes study selection, categorization (study design, research question, COVID phase), and quality appraisal, but no methods for preparing data for presentation or synthesis, such as handling missing summary statistics or data conversions, are reported anywhere. The closest statement, 'we classified study designs according to the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality', concerns study design classification rather than data preparation for synthesis.

elements.quote: Table I, II, and III synthesize the distribution of selected studies by geographical area (Table I), limitations of functioning of rehabilitation interest (LFRI), disease phase and rehabilitation setting (Table II), research question, and study design (Table III).
elements.reason: Tables are used and their content is evident, but this appears in the results, and the Methods section contains no description of the tabular structures used to display results (e.g., supplementary tables of study characteristics) or how they were constructed.

elements.quote: Figure 3.-Distribution of criteria for quality appraisal of observational studies according to JBI checklists for cross-sectional (A), cohort (B) and prevalence (inception cohort) (C) studies.
elements.reason: Figures (PRISMA flow diagram, RoB bar charts, JBI appraisal figures) are presented, but the Methods section does not describe any graphical methods used to display or synthesize results.

elements.quote: Table I, II, and III synthesize the distribution of selected studies by geographical area (Table I)... research question, and study design (Table III).
elements.reason: The tables are grouped by topic (geography, LFRI/phase/setting, research question/design), but no basis for ordering or grouping individual studies within the tables or figures is reported in the Methods.

elements.quote: Figure 2.-Distribution of Risks of Bias in the included Randomized Controlled trials, according to the Cochrane Risk of Bias (RoB 1) tool.
elements.reason: Only standard displays are used (PRISMA flow diagram and conventional RoB/JBI stacked bar charts); no non-standard graphs are employed, so no rationale is required.

elements.quote: This third edition still provides a narrative synthesis of findings, as a meta-analysis is not applicable due to the high heterogeneity of the studies.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was performed, so no software or packages were needed or reported.

elements.reason: The planned meta-analysis is explicitly judged inappropriate and the reason (high study heterogeneity) is reported; also confirmed in text_14: 'metasynthesis was not possible due to study heterogeneity.'

No methods for exploring heterogeneity (subgroup analysis, meta-regression, or narrative exploration methods) are reported. The review states only that meta-analysis was not applicable due to heterogeneity.
No subgroup analysis or meta-regression factors, levels, or expected directions of effect modification are reported.
No mention of study-level variables or within-study contrasts, as no such analyses were described.
No methods for comparing subgroup effects are reported.
No informal heterogeneity-exploration methods with factors and levels are described; the review only reports a narrative synthesis without specifying heterogeneity-exploration methods.
No analyses of heterogeneity are reported at all, so none are identified as pre-specified or post hoc.

elements.reason: No sensitivity analyses are described anywhere in the retrieved evidence; the review used a narrative synthesis with no meta-analysis and no sensitivity analyses reported.
Since no sensitivity analyses are reported at all, there is no identification of any as non-pre-specified.

No methods for assessing risk of bias due to missing results (e.g., funnel plots, Egger tests, or other reporting-bias assessments) are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence. The review reports risk-of-bias/quality appraisal (RoB 1, JBI checklists) but nothing specifically addressing reporting biases or missing results in a synthesis.

No reporting-bias assessment tool is used or described; only Cochrane RoB 1 and JBI checklists for study-level risk of bias/methodological quality are reported, with no domains or overall judgement process for reporting bias due to missing results.
No reporting-bias tool is used or adapted, so no adaptations could be described.
No newly developed reporting-bias tool is used or mentioned.

elements.quote: Two review authors (C.A., V.I.) independently appraised the quality of studies and resolved disagreements by consensus; in the case of persistent disagreement, a third review author was consulted (P.C.) and the disagreement resolved by consensus.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers (two), their independence, and the disagreement-resolution procedure (consensus, third author arbitration) are explicitly reported for the bias/quality appraisal process.
No processes for obtaining or confirming information from study investigators (e.g., regarding unreported outcomes) are reported.
No automation tools for reporting-bias assessment are described or mentioned.

elements.quote: We also expanded the evaluation of the quality of evidence using JBI checklists 8 to appraise the methodological quality of observational studies and the Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool (RoB 1) to appraise methodological quality for randomized-controlled clinical trials (RCTs).
elements.reason: The manuscript describes tools for risk-of-bias/methodological quality appraisal (JBI checklists, RoB 1), but no tool or system for assessing certainty (or confidence) in the body of evidence (e.g., GRADE) is reported.

No factors or criteria for assessing certainty in the body of evidence are reported; only risk-of-bias appraisal criteria via JBI checklists and RoB 1 are described, which does not constitute certainty assessment.
No decision rules or interpretation of certainty levels (e.g., high/moderate/low/very high) are described anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No certainty assessment of the body of evidence was performed; the review used only narrative synthesis with study-level quality appraisal, so review-specific certainty considerations do not apply.
No certainty-assessment system was used or adapted; only standard JBI and RoB 1 quality-appraisal tools were applied.

elements.quote: Two review authors (C.A., V.I.) independently appraised the quality of studies and resolved disagreements by consensus; in the case of persistent disagreement, a third review author was consulted (P.C.) and the disagreement resolved by consensus.
elements.reason: Number of reviewers, independence, and disagreement-resolution procedures are reported, but only for study-level quality/risk-of-bias appraisal, not for certainty assessment of the body of evidence, which was not performed.
No certainty assessment was performed, so processes for obtaining or confirming information from investigators for certainty purposes do not apply.
No automation tools for certainty assessment are mentioned; no certainty assessment was performed.

elements.quote: Supplementary Digital Material 2 (Supplementary Table I) describes the output of the quality appraisal of each included study, grouped by design
elements.reason: Results of quality appraisal are reported in supplementary tables and figures, but no methods for reporting certainty-assessment results (e.g., Summary of Findings tables or GRADE certainty ratings) are described.
No standard phrases incorporating certainty of evidence are used, since no certainty assessment was conducted.

elements.quote: We identified 7496 citations (3699 after removal of duplicates) from the databases. After title and abstract screening, we evaluated 120 studies
elements.reason: Text reports records identified (7496), after duplicate removal (3699), and screened; the PRISMA flow diagram (text_7, figure_2) additionally shows records excluded at title/abstract screening (n=3579).

elements.quote: full-text articles assessed for eligibility (n.=120) ... full-text articles excluded, with reasons (n.=95)
elements.reason: The flow diagram reports the number sought/assessed (120), not retrieved is not addressed, and 95 full-text exclusions are labeled 'with reasons', but the actual exclusion reasons are not enumerated in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: we evaluated 120 studies and included 25 in the narrative synthesis (Figure 1)
elements.reason: The number of included studies (25) is reported in text and in the flow diagram ('studies included in qualitative synthesis (n.=25)'); included reports are effectively the 25 papers.
No retrieved evidence mentions ongoing studies or associated reports.
